response.sql: SELECT major.college, SUM(income.amount) as total_income, SUM(income.amount) / (SELECT SUM(income.amount) FROM income JOIN member ON income.link_to_member = member.member_id JOIN major ON member.link_to_major = major.major_id) as fraction FROM income JOIN member ON income.link_to_member = member.member_id JOIN major ON member.link_to_major = major.major_id GROUP BY major.college

assumptions.assumption: "Total income" in the fraction denominator refers to the sum of income records that successfully link through member to major, not the global sum of all income records. This means income from members without a major (if link_to_major is NULL) is excluded from both numerator and denominator, making fractions sum to 1.0.

alternatives.interpretation: "Total income" refers to the global sum of all income records, including those from members without majors. Each college's fraction represents its share of the global total. This interpretation uses the same linked query but divides by the unconditional sum of all income.
alternatives.sql: SELECT major.college, SUM(income.amount) as total_income, SUM(income.amount) / (SELECT SUM(amount) FROM income) as fraction FROM income JOIN member ON income.link_to_member = member.member_id JOIN major ON member.link_to_major = major.major_id GROUP BY major.college
